utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we invite the Prosecution to call its next witness, which will be Mr. Theunens, I was informed that there were a few procedural matters the Prosecution would like to raise. Perhaps, Mr. Weber, I go through my list and see to what extent that already covers some of your problems. I do understand that the Prosecution wanted to tender only selected portion of some of the documents in relation to Mr. Theunens, and for that purpose has uploaded into e-court documents replacing the ones earlier uploaded, and that would -- the exhibit numbers would remain the same, but the 65 ter numbers would be the old ones, but then .1 added to the original 65 ter number indicating that it's just an excerpt of the original one, and this would be true for P1014, P1015, P1019, P1023, P1027, P1031, P1032, P1074, P1177, P1376, and P1412. The corresponding 65 ter numbers would be, and I follow the same order: 65 ter 3847.1, 65 ter 3857.1, 65 ter 3852.1, 65 ter 3858.1, 65 ter 1886.1, 65 ter 3853.1, 65 ter 3866.1, 65 ter 3845.1, 65 ter 4206.1 65 ter 3829.1, and 65 ter 4117.1. Mr. Weber, was this one of the issues you wanted to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for addressing it. The numbers read in are correct, and yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then Madam Registrar is invited and is permitted to replace the original 65 ter numbers related to these exhibit numbers by the .1 versions of those documents. Madam Registrar, is this sufficient information for you?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then a second matter is that the Prosecution has requested leave to add Mr. Theunens CV to its Rule 65 ter exhibit list, which was filed on the 13th of August, 2010. There are no objections from the Defence, therefore leave is granted to add the CV of Mr. Theunens to the 65 ter exhibit list. Then I have two more items we should deal with before we hear the testimony of Mr. Theunens. These two items are related -- these are, as a matter of fact, are elements in the history preceding the determination by the Chamber of the date on which the Chamber would hear the testimony of Mr. Theunens. I put on the record that an e-mail was sent by Chamber's staff on the 7th of September, 2010, informing the parties that the deadline for responses to the Simatovic request for postponement of testimony of Prosecution expert witness Reynaud Theunens, a request which was filed on the 6th of September, 2010, that these deadlines had been shortened to close of business on the 10th of September, 2010. The second element in the history preceding the determination of the timing of the hearing of Mr. Theunens's testimony was an e-mail of the 17th of September, 2010, sent by Chamber's staff informing the parties that the Chamber had decided that the testimony of Mr. Theunens should not be bifurcated and should not take place before the last week of October 2010. These were the urgent items I had on my list to be dealt with before Mr. Theunens enters the courtroom. Anything else, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Prosecution wanted to address a couple of matters and also put some items on the record. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Over the weekend the Stanisic and Simatovic Defence communicated the exhibits that will be opposed by each Defence from the chart of exhibits for Mr. Theunens. There are approximately 65 exhibits being opposed by either one or both of the Defence teams. If acceptable to the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution is willing to defer discussion on any objections to the opposed exhibits until after the testimony of the witness and tender today only those exhibits which are not opposed by either Defence. This would be done in order to make optimum use of the available court time this week. That's the first matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In principle I see the good sense in that. On the other hand, I think it would be important for Your Honours to appreciate with certain exhibits what our objection is before we launch into cross-examining Mr. Theunens on the basis of those objections. I think Your Honours will be guided by a very brief description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what we now have is we have a series of documents, a small portion of them contested, Mr. Weber says I will not tender them at this moment. Now, you'd say you would like to raise -- at least raise matters in relation to those exhibits. So that's part of the contested ones, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We've only -- the Stanisic Defence have only objected to around, I think, ten exhibits, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please identify those ten. If you just write down the numbers on a little piece of paper then I take it that Mr. Weber, if -- may I take it if you want to cross-examine the witness on them that they have to be in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're not saying it's -- because you also could, of course, examine the witness just on matters of relevance and say it's totally irrelevant. Do you not agree, Mr. Theunens? And then say therefore they should not be admitted but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, perhaps I should be careful about what I say. We do object to the admissibility of around ten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And we say the Court should exclude them without further consideration, at least some of them. And we indicate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So what we now have a list of those documents uncontested tendered by Mr. Weber, which therefore I take it are ready for being admitted, and then we have a number which perhaps we -- I think the others are -- numbers are assigned and not yet marked for identification, but if we would know which ten they are then we could mark them for identification, and if you give the numbers to Mr. Weber then he could --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: He has them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He has them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The exhibits are -- part of the exhibits are presently marked for identification. The Prosecution appreciates the position of the Defence and believes that they should have an opportunity to state their objections for the record, and also have the opportunity to cross-examine on them. We're just proposing this measure for the sake of the scheduling and for convenience. We would obviously like to be heard also eventually on the objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the objections if you have raised them during cross-examination, and I take it that Mr. Weber would have an opportunity to further explain that, because -- but let's not do that out of the blue but on the basis of knowing what the objections are.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. May I while I'm on my feet introduce Mr. Gosnell to the Court who is presently our consultant but hopefully more very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gosnell, welcome in this courtroom. Mr. Bakrac, any response to the suggestion made by Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, Your Honour. I have heard your position now, and I am going to adjust to that, of course. I just don't understand one thing, Mr. Weber got to the number of the document that we disagree with, that is 59 -- or, rather, 62. That is what is in dispute, and we have to check three documents with our client, and we need to check something as well. I'm going to submit a list to you. I provided it to Mr. Weber on Friday, and I'm going to give you a list of these documents that are in dispute. I'll try to do that during the next break, and then during the examination we are going to deal with these documents that are still in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you'll understand that I don't like reading long lists of numbers, but I'm certainly not going to read the very, very long lists of numbers. So therefore, could the parties provide to Madam Registrar already the list indicating which ones are the tendered ones, the contested ones, and contested by which party so that we have an overview of that, and then we will later find a way of putting this appropriately on the record by other means than by reading those lists. Anything else, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Two other matters that we'd like to put on the record. On the 22nd of October, 2010, the Prosecution provided Mr. Theunens with a binder containing an unmarked copy of his report dated 30 June 2007 with exhibit numbers in the footnotes. It is the understanding of the Prosecution that the witness has placed tabs, made highlights, and made notations of cross-references within the report. Prosecution has not reviewed these markings. The witness has this binder with him and has indicated that it would facilitate and expedite his testimony before the Trial Chamber. Apparently this approach has been done in the past with this witness. The Prosecution has also provided the witness with two binders containing exhibits for the witness to review at the request of the Stanisic Defence. The next matter that the Prosecution want to place on the record was just that we provided the Chamber and Defence prior to the testimony of the witness with binders containing the report of the witness with exhibits -- exhibit numbers in the footnotes, the curriculum vitae of the witness, and a chart of the exhibits which was filed last week. The Prosecution will be referring to these materials during the testimony of Mr. Theunens. If anyone in the courtroom would like another copy or a copy of this binder, the Prosecution does have extra binders available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, one final matter is about the CV of Mr. Theunens. We just decided that leave was granted to add it to the 65 ter list, but it has no exhibit number yet, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It does not. The Prosecution has uploaded it under 65 ter 5812.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 5812. And since there were no objections against adding it to the 65 ter list, may I also assume that there is no objection against the admission into evidence of 65 ter 5812? Then, Madam Registrar, 65 ter 5812 receives.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1574, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1574, Mr. Theunens's CV is admitted into evidence. Then -- yes. One issue totally related to what we've dealt with until now. Mr. Jordash, did you have an opportunity to speak with Mr. Stanisic about scheduling of tomorrow afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I did Your Honour, and his preference would be to return to the UNDU if possible, please, between the break -- or in the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And he does not oppose against having at the most two sessions in the afternoon, a little bit of a late start, because tomorrow morning we'll have available until 11.30, which means that we will sit from 9.00 to 10.00, have a break from 10.00 to 10.30 and then sit from 10.30 to 11.30. That would be the moment where transportation back, and I know that that takes some time, could be arranged for. We would then -- I would prefer to start a bit later so that we have more time over the lunch break where Mr. Stanisic will be during I think at least one hour will be in his cell, then to start for example at 3.00 until 4.15, and then from quarter to 5.00 to 6.00, leave it two sessions, which would mean in the whole of the day four and a half hours effective court time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then -- yes. I was just informed, Mr. Weber, that the Prosecution was not yet informed about these plans. No final decision has been taken. The reason why you have not been informed is that we first wanted to find out what practical problems there might be at all. Second thing we wanted to find out is whether the condition of Mr. Stanisic would oppose to any such thing, and it's only since one minute now that I know that after Mr. Jordash has consulted with his client that there is no opposition from the Stanisic Defence that now I address the Prosecution and the Simatovic Defence where we are, unfortunately, limited in time tomorrow morning. It's not the Chamber's decision, but there's no other possibility, to have a session between 3.00 and 6.00 tomorrow in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Simatovic Defence also understands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then hereby Madam Registrar is invited to inform all the units, sections, whoever has to make this all possible, to inform them that as far as the Chamber is concerned, we would sit from 9.00 to 11.30, and then from 3.00 to 6.00. It was of no use to inform you any earlier if for other reasons it would not have worked anyhow. Having dealt with all these practical matters, anything else to be raised before Mr. Theunens enters the courtroom? No? Then could the usher please escort Mr. Theunens into the courtroom. I add immediately to what I earlier said is that there is some conflict in the scheduling of the Judges as well. So it all depends whether this will finally work or not whether the Chamber would finally decide for the afternoon whether it would be appropriate to sit under Rule 15 bis. That's one of the remaining issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Usually I start by saying Mr. Theunens, I presume, but let's be fair. I've seen you before, Mr. Theunens, so therefore, good afternoon, Mr. Theunens. Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Theunens. Mr. Theunens, before we start your testimony, I'd like to inform you about some scheduling issues. We intend to sit this afternoon. We intend to sit on Thursday in the afternoon and on Friday in the afternoon. However, tomorrow, Wednesday, the 27th, in order to use as much time as possible, and since we are facing all kind of practical problems, it is for certain that we'll sit in the morning hours, that is from 9.00 to 11.30, and it is likely that we sit in the afternoon from 3.00 to 6.00, but this has not yet been finally determined. Just for your information. Mr. Weber, are you ready to start your examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you'll now first be examined by Mr. Weber, who, it may not come as a surprise, is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1574 in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, while the exhibit is being brought up before you, could you please introduce yourself to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Reynaud Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, does the CV that now appears before you correctly indicate your personal information on the top of page 1?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this CV also accurately represent your educational background?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to your position with UNIFIL from April 2009 onward, does this CV accurately describe your present responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of this exhibit shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to your past positions as an intelligence analyst with the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, Office of the Prosecutor, the Belgian Ministry of Defence, and the Belgian Armed Forces, does this CV accurately describe your past responsibilities and duties in these positions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What do the acronyms SGRS, and IE represent?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, SGRS stance for Service General du Renseignement et de la Securite, which in English means general service for intelligence and security, and IE stands for the I for intelligence or information, and the E for exploitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your curriculum vitae indicates that between September 1992 and June 1999, you were a Balkans analyst at the SGRS and performed assessments of political, military, and economic developments in the former Yugoslavia at both the operational and strategic level. Could you please explain these assessments along with their frequency and scope?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, together with my colleagues we prepared daily analysis of the events of the past 24 hours. They were intended for the operations staff in order to assist them in planning the operations of Belgian peacekeepers in the former Yugoslavia. We also prepared weekly analysis, written analysis, in addition to this daily and written -- excuse me, to these daily and weekly written analysis we would also prepare ad hoc documents. For example, the Ministry of Defence would attend meetings with colleagues of neighbouring countries or on a multilateral level his office would request such a document. It would also prepare on the basis of these written analyses oral briefings on a daily, weekly and ad hoc basis for the same addressees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, most of your previous testimony before this Tribunal as an expert witness is listed under section 7 of your CV. Could you please briefly explain the scope of your expert analysis and testimony in the five cases that are listed under section 7?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, for four of these five cases the testimony and the underlying report dealt with senior Serb suspects, by my role consisted of providing an overall background focused on doctrine JNA SFRY Armed Forces, and then to look at -- I mean to study on the basis of the written evidence that was available to study and analyse to what extent this de jure doctrine was applied in practice, and also to identify other relevant issues as defined by the senior trial attorneys who would issue the tasking to me. The fifth report, the case of Ante Gotovina, Ivan Cermak, and Mladen Markac, the tasking was similar but in this case it applied to senior members of the Croatian Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Have you recently testified in any cases before this Tribunal and if so could you please tell us the case name.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, two weeks ago I testified in the review hearing in the so-called Vukovar case, review hearing concerning Mr. Veselin Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you complete a military analysis in this case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Your Honours, I prepared a report which is now in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the scope of your analysis in this report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The scope, Your Honours, is -- is discussed in the first section scope and executive summary, and basically I have tried to do two things, first of all to provide the military background, as I mentioned earlier today what I would call due Jure, i.e., SFRY doctrinal armed forces doctrinal issues which I considered relevant in the context of this case as well as look at how this doctrine was implemented, call that the de facto aspects, and in addition to that I then analysed the military role -- or the military aspects, I'm sorry, the military aspects of the role of Mr. Jovica Stanisic and Mr. Frenki Simatovic during the time period that was given to me, i.e., from, say, early 1999 -- 1991 to December 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does your report analyse the organisational structure of the Ministry of Interior of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. My report does not look into that aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What methodology did you apply to the review and selection of documents in this case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The methodology I applied is generally known as the intelligence cycle whereby there are four discrete phases, direction, collection, processing, and dissemination, and whereby in the processing face which is often defined as the analysis phase, there are five steps. I mean, I can give them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the Prosecution would like to discuss this with you. What occurred during the direction phase in this case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Basically direction consists of determining the focus of the analysis or of the research project, and there I was tasked by Ms. Brehmeier in the course of spring 2007 to prepare a military report for this case. I -- in response I prepared a draft table of contents which was basically -- which was mainly based on -- on reports I had done for other cases involving senior Serb suspects. I tried to expand it and also to focus it on the specific aspects of this case. I submitted a draft table of contents to Ms. Brehmeier, she agreed, and I used that then as the direction for my further research.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please explain how you completed the collection phase of your analysis in this case?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, during the collection I gathered information whereby I confined myself to written information, i.e., again, looking at the scope doctrinal regulations, military orders, military reports, open sources, and any related documents, and I conducted searches in the databases that were available in the Office of the Prosecutor, as well as in some case on the internet in order to identify or to obtain additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were any limits placed on your access to materials by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The Office of the Prosecutor did not impose or place any limits to my access to material.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How were open-source materials in the form of books, news articles, and recorded public statements relevant to your analysis?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I mean, traditionally in intelligence it is said that 80 per cent of the material originates from open sources. Of course when dealing with open sources one has to be very careful, and again that is also part of the process I explained earlier, the intelligence cycle, because obviously there is the risk of barriers and so on and so on, but also in this particular context of the conflict in the former Yugoslavia, many senior officials who played, yeah, an important role during the conflict published memoirs or other books that covered their activities. Of course, and again this is part of the process, when dealing with such information one looks for, among other things, for corroboration from other material, and there I think in the Office of the Prosecutor we are in a privileged report because we have access original documents and original reports, i.e., not secondary sources but original documents and, yeah, open source can also provide context and they can provide lead material.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please explain the processing phase and the steps you utilised to select and categorise materials for your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: In the processing phase basically there are five steps identified. The first one is collation. Just means that you organise the material that you have available in a manner that it's easy to be consulted. Can be that you make separate databases, spreadsheets, binders, whatever. Next and in my view much more important is the evaluation phase -- sorry, the evaluation step where we look at two aspects, the reliability of the source and the credibility of the information. Obviously -- oh no, it's important -- sorry, it's important notice that a reliable source can provide information of low credibility and vice versa, and again this comes back to what I said earlier with the corroboration. After the evaluation, we're going to analyse the material, which means that we're going to subject the information we have in front of us to a mental process in order to identify relevant facts for subsequent interpretation. This interpretation means that you will confront what you know with the new information, and it could be that it basically says the same or that it shows something different, and then at the end in the integration phase a step -- excuse me, it's a step you're going to combine the two and you draw conclusions. So interpretation basically you're going to say, well, so what. What does it mean? What does this new information mean? And then of course then it will have an impact or it will change your body of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did you assess the reliability of the materials that you selected and cited in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Reliability applies to the source, and again I think -- I mean it's the same as research -- other academic research or academic research is concerned, i.e., you're going to look at for example what is the reputation of a source. If you have a source where there's doubtful reputation, well you may handle the information provided by that source with care. If you have a source with a good reputation, you may have more trust in the information that source provide but as I said before, a reliable source can still provide information of low credibility. A second aspect would be what is the relation between the source and the fact or the event that is included in the information? If you have, for example, in this situation if you have -- if you have information provided by what I would call the opposing side, you may handle that with more care than when a unit commander is talking about the activities of his own units. The relation may also be -- may also cover the time aspects, i.e., is it contemporaneous information or information has become available much later. Is the source the first source or is he or she basing himself on what somebody else has reported and so on and so on. So there are various criteria you apply to determine the reliability of a source.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please explain the dissemination phase of the intelligence cycle.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Dissemination basically means that you submit the product of your work, i.e., your analysis in this case in written form to the one who has requested that for you -- from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Prior to the completion of the dissemination phase of your report in this case, did the Office of the Prosecutor instruct you to revise or include any analysis contained in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The only kind of guidance I received is that there were certain aspects where I wasn't sure whether that was -- I was expected to cover that or the MUP expert was expected to cover that. So I asked Ms. Brehmeier whether I would have to cover it or whether somebody else did it and okay then I received an answer to the question, but there was no intervention in the contents of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You mention that you have a binder here today in court. Does this binder contain a copy of your report and would this assist you and facilitate your testimony before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's a copy of my report I received from the Office of the Prosecutor with exhibit numbers or P numbers MFIs added, and since I arrived here I have been reading and marking it up to facilitate my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution requests that during the course of your testimony that you refer to the exhibit numbers as much as possible when you're referring to an exhibit in order so that we could have a clear record of the exhibit that you're referring to. You've explained the overview and executive summary already in your report. Following the executive summary, there is a table of contents. Could you please explain how you'd structure your report using the table of contents.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It refers to what I explained earlier to the scope so that the report stands with the background section which focuses on the main doctrinal issues of SFRY Armed Forces, the JNA, consisting of the JNA and the TO as well as volunteers. I also have a very briefly touched upon armed forces of the Republic of Serbia. And in the second part I discuss the military aspects of the role of Mr. Jovica Stanisic and Frenki Simatovic in the conflict in Croatia, and the third part discusses the same role, however for the conflict or what Bosnia-Herzegovina is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution tenders the report of Mr. Theunens. We are willing at this time to tender into evidence. We've uploaded it under 65 ter 5811.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage we would invite the court to MFI it until after cross-examination, and then we might have submission at that stage as to its admissibility depending upon what Mr. Theunens says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Likewise. The Simatovic Defence proposes the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you live with a solution in which we do not start arguing about admissibility until after we've heard the testimony of Mr. Theunens and that we for the time being MFI the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And 5811, is that the copy of the report where the P numbers are included?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the newest version with the blue P numbers, at least on the screen they appear to me as blue. Madam Registrar, 65 ter 5811 would be MFI'd under what number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be number P1575, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1575 keeps the status of marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In sections 1 and 2 on pages 2 to 79 of part 1 of your report, you analyse the legislative and doctrinal framework of the armed forces of the SFRY between the years of 1974 to 1990, and also the Republic of Serbia between 1990 and 1991. Could you please explain how the materials you analysed in these two sections relate to your subsequent analysis of events which occurred between 1991 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: This -- I mean, doctrine or military doctrine is defined as the set of rules according to which armed forces operate or are supposed to operate, and in this regard -- in context of this report for me, and again this was not the first time I looked at it, I started with it -- with this when I arrived at -- I'm sorry, I started to include these aspects in expert reports here within the OTP already from the first report I drafted, report for the trial of Mr. Slobodan Milosevic. I considered this doctrine essential in order to understand the subsequent events that are discussed in part 2 and part 3, i.e., to understand what are these armed forces, what is their mission, what -- how is command and control organised, what are their duties in relation to international humanitarian law. Something like volunteers is a concept that is popping up or is appearing systematically throughout the conflict. I thought it was important to see whether there was any legal basis for this concept, and if yes what was this legal basis. And I then used this doctrinal and legal basis to review the actual events on the basis of military reports, military orders, reports from the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia, instructions from the republic from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia as well as other documents in order to describe and analyse the activities of a number of units and groups during the conflict in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is an ad hoc formation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: With ad hoc I mean that the formation or the -- or the unit or the group is established for a specific mission. I should rephrase that. Is established to carry out a specific mission in a specific area during a specific time period, and it is established because it consists of several sub-units or elements which outside the framework of the specific mission do not necessarily operate together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to JNA military manuals, in the 1981 JNA military lexicon how were these ad hoc formations designated?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I mean, it's not only in the lexicon because the lexicon is just a dictionary without, I would say, legal implications for military officers but also the regulations I reviewed, and you can find them back in the first part, they define even strategic groupings, but I haven't addressed them in my report because they are in my view not relevant for the -- in the context of this report but there are strategic groupings. There are operational groups. There are tactical groups, assault detachments and assault groups, and the names obviously -- or the how you call it categorisation depends on the size and the composition of these ad hoc units, but they all have in common that they're established for a specific mission in a specific area during a specific time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to section 2 of part 1 on page 70, you state on this page of your report that: "Article 118 of the 1991 Law on Defence of the Republic of Serbia implies that the Serbian volunteer paramilitary formations, including groups led by Dragan and Arkan, or other formations that were controlled by or linked otherwise to the MUP of Serbia could only be set up, including recruitment of their members, and exist with the authorisation and approval of the Serbian authorities in general and the MUP of Serbia in particular." My question to you is how did you reach this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this conclusion is based on the material I reviewed during the preparation of this report, and in addition, of course, to all the documents you can find in part 2 and part 3 when I discuss the activities of -- of these groups in particular Dragan's people and Arkan's people as well as other groups which are discussed in part 2 and part 3, and when I looked at -- at those documents in -- in one hand -- or one side and on the other hand Article 118, which is very straightforward, it means that these volunteers/paramilitary - and just to clarify I use paramilitary here as formations not foreseen by the law which act in a military manner or are organised in a military manner or conduct operations that -- or conduct military operations, sorry - that they were established, and since based on the material I -- I reviewed they existed for several years and after they were involved in Croatia and their involvement was very much publicised, they became also involved in the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina implied for me that there was an approval of their existence over several years, and again based then on the -- on the duty of the ministry interior as well as other ministries in the republic of Serbia to enforce the law, and again that would also imply enforcing Article 118, I could only conclude that the ministry of -- that the authorities at Republic of Serbia as well as the Ministry of Interior approved not only the establishment but also the existence of such groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Turning to section 3 on pages 80 to 120 of part 1 of your report, in this section you discuss the legal and factual background of Serbian volunteers and paramilitaries. Did you reach any conclusions as to which volunteer or paramilitary units were controlled by or related otherwise to the Ministry of Interior of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and maybe just to clarify I think the word "control," I haven't used it in a strict military sense, but since we were looking at the situation which I would qualify as very much ad hoc, i.e., that the existing legislation, I'm talking about legislation that existed prior to August 1991, did not foresee the existence of such units, i.e., nonmilitary units carrying out military operations. We can see and again that's discussed further on in that section that both on the level of the Republic of Serbia as well as on the level of the SFRY, additional decrees or laws are adopted to legalise the existence of these volunteer/paramilitary groups. And again looking at the material that is included in part 2 and 3, I could only conclude that these groups existed with the approval -- and when I say these groups, okay, the focus is here on groups like Dragan and Draganovci, Arkan and the Serbian Volunteer Guards, as well as a group that became known as the Special Purpose Unit of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, often identified as -- as Red Berets, yeah, obviously that these groups existed -- that these groups existed with the -- sorry, with the knowledge and the approval of the ministry of interior, and even more that they were controlled or linked otherwise by the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to discuss some examples of documents which you reference in your report. Could the Prosecution please have the first page of P1062 marked for identification shown to the witness. The Prosecution requests that this document not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, in order to avoid whatever conclusion, when you earlier referred to section 3 starting on page 80, you had on your mind the page numbered 80 of the first part of the report. Is that -- that means that the -- more or less the summary has its own numbering. Then we are talking here about the -- about one of the report, because the numbering of part 2 and part 3 is different. We often refer to e-court page numbers, but this certainly is not an e-court number. So could you -- if you use actual page numbers in the hard copies, could you always indicate in what section were the first, the second, or the third we are so that we -- that those who will read the transcript are able to find what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. I will try to make clear at least for the time being the page number within the section and part of the report, and as I go on, I will try to incorporate the e-court pages if it's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- which would then result in second part or hard copy, second part, page so-and-so, e-court page so-and-so, because the e-court numbering goes on to 426.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course I could read out the ERN number of the page if that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, for purposes of searching, I think e-court and hard copy pages are of assistance, whereas ERN numbers may be of less assistance. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the document that is now before you is Exhibit P1062, marked for identification. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a report, information report drafted by the security administration of the SFRY Armed Forces with the title "Some Information on Daniel Snedden, Australian Citizen, alias Captain Dragan," and it's sent to the federal secretary for peoples or for national defence army general Veljko Kadijevic, and as well as a number of other addressees but they are not visible on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What information is contained in the first paragraph of this report which describes a relationship between Daniel Snedden, aka Captain Dragan, and the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The first paragraph, Your Honours, discusses the role of Dragan in the training of what is called a special unit of the SAO Krajina MUP in Golubic, and -- and there's also reference to his alleged connections with the -- with organs of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia who are engaged in the same mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have the footnote on the bottom of this page. Which individuals from the MUP of Serbia are in this footnote which the text states were engaged in the same mission as Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, two individuals are mentioned. First Franko Simatovic, also known as Frenki, and secondly, Dragoljub Filipovic also known as Fico.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know how Dragoljub Filipovic was also known as based on the other materials you reviewed in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have seen Fico and Fica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 in the English and B/C/S versions of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this report indicate how the DB of Serbia initially made operative contact with Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honours. It indicates that they were first monitoring his behaviour and that subsequently afterward, after he altered his previous orientation they established operative contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would now like to show you Exhibit P992 in evidence. This document that is now before you, could you please identify it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is a request by Captain Dragan to the Ministry of Interior -- excuse me, to the command of the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this document, it refers to the Bubanj Potok centre. Do you know where this is located?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The Bubanj Potok centre is located near Belgrade in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How does Captain Dragan define his status according to this request?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah, Dragan expresses a request, I think, to kind of maintain the image he had maintained by then, I mean by the date of the document, and he refers to what he identifies as obligations towards the state security of the Republic of Serbia whereby he underlines that his activities in relation with the TO of the Republic of Serbia should be fully in accordance with these obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P1069 marked for identification shown to the witness. This document is referred to in e-court pages 120 to 121.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, these are the minutes of a meeting between ministers of defence of the Republic of Serbia Tomislav Simovic and Captain Dragan. What topics were discussed at this meeting between Captain Dragan and Minister Simovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah. I mean there are three topics which are identified on the first page. The work of the Captain Dragan Fund, last engagement of Captain Dragan, and his -- the possibilities of his further engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the minutes in both English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, directing your attention to the middle of page 2 of the English version, does this document also indicate who invited Captain Dragan to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes. According to this document he was invited by the state security of the Republic of Serbia to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to these minutes, who was Captain Dragan collaborating with in -- when he came to the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: According to the document, there is mention of a Stanisic. Now, based on -- on the context we are talking about, I concluded that this is Mr. Jovica Stanisic, as well as Radmilo Bogdanovic, who is also a minister of interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this document continue to describe any assignment that Captain Dragan had after he arrived?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed. Reference is made to the training of volunteers as well as activities in co-operation with Milan Martic. So the minister of the interior of the SAO Krajina at the time and Milan Babic the prime minister of the SAO Krajina at the time, and these activities as they are described here are coherent in what we see in other documents that are discussed in my report when I discovered this document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on the content of these minutes and other exhibits you reference in your report, can you determine the approximate date of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my report, and this is part 1, page 99, footnote 278, I state that this meeting must have taken place before December 1991, because on the previous page in P1066, Mr. Simovic -- I mean General Simovic, who was then the minister of defence of the Republic of Serbia, provides a written answer to a question by Vojislav Seselj, a question he asked in his position as member of the Assembly, on the activities of Dragan, and this is P1066 MFI. There Simovic refers to his proposal that Dragan would train volunteers, Serb Krajina volunteers, in Bubanj Potok within the existing system.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of this -- of the English version. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, Mr. Weber, could you also have a look at the clock and find a suitable within the next two or three minutes to have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What conclusion was reached by Minister Simovic at the end of these minutes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah. The conclusion is that -- I mean, for the minister that it's not a question whether Dragan should be engaged, i.e., in the training of volunteers, or -- but actually how this should be done, and he refers to the need for additional consultations on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it's okay with the Trial Chamber, this would be a suitable time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break, and we will resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apologies for the late start. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit D31 in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, on pages 105 to 107 of part 1 of your report, e-court page 128 to 130, in your analysis of Arkan's relationship to the MUP of Serbia, you discuss intelligence reports from both the JNA and VJ security organs. These are exhibits P327, P328, D31 in evidence, and P1061, P1077, P1078, and P1079 marked for identification. Directing your attention to Exhibit D31 which is now before you, could you please identify this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a report or information by the security organ of the 1st Military District dated the 19th of October, 1991, which is submitted to three addressees identified at the top of the page. The first department of the security administration, the third department of the security administration, as well as the security organs of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the lower portion of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this report indicate who is supplying Arkan with weapons and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed. According to this report, weapons, ammunition, and mines and explosives are, according to what Arkan stated to the -- the person who was in contact with him, supplied by the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this report, what is Arkan doing with those weapons and ammunition that are being supplied to him?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Arkan is reportedly distributing them to local Serb TO staffs in a number of municipalities in Eastern Slavonia, Erdut, Sarvas, and Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You just stated on page 30, lines 15 and 16, according to the person who is in contact with him. According to this information here, who is the source of the information about these weapons and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I think I answered the question that the weapons and ammunition originate from the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, but according to this report, who is the source of the information?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Ah, I'm sorry. It's 2nd Lieutenant Goran Blagojevic, who is a security organ in the Savska Venac local TO staff, and okay the Bratsvo Jedinstvo Bridge is one of the three bridges -- I mean, it's not in the document but I was stationed during a certain time period in Eastern Slavonia, it's one of the three passages over the Danube separating Slavonia, Branjevo, Western Srem from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Actually, directing your attention to the paragraph that begins "during several consecutive contacts with Arkan he stated."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does -- what does this statement indicate to you as to the source of the information as contained in this report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: That Arkan provided information to the -- I mean, I oversaw that, that Arkan provide the information to the 2nd lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What relationship, if any, did the Ministry of Defence of Serbia have with the JNA or the VJ?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I have not analysed that for this report, but when I prepared a similar report for the trial of Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, basically the Ministry of Defence acted as a -- as a facilitator to assist the local Serbs in Krajina and also Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem with organising or setting up arms structures, as well as recruiting volunteers whereby requests were regularly sent by these local Serbs to the Ministry of Defence, who would then -- of the Republic of Serbia, I'm sorry, who would then forward them to I think that some kind of a co-ordination body was organised which would then forward them to the JNA. And some of these requests may also have been forwarded by the republic of -- excuse me, by the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia to the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1077 marked for identification. The Prosecution requests that this document not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, with respect to the next exhibit, could you please not refer to the name of the source of the information in this report. Could you please identify the exhibit and the subject matter of the report that now appears before you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It's another information report compiled by security organs. It's identified there as -- I mean at the top left corner is 1st Army, but it should actually been -- oops -- the 1st Military District, security organ, 19th of November, 1992, and it is sent to a number of addressees in the Main Staff -- or actually it should be the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, as well as security organ of the 1st Army. I think there is some -- some confusion at that time, because I remember the VJ was restructuring from military districts to armies and that's why there seems to be some confusion with the author whether it's a military district or an army. I mean, it's just a detail but it deals with or it covers indications re: the establishment of what is defined as a Serbian Army centre as well as criminal activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the B/C/S original and page 3 of the English version of this exhibit, specifically the top half the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what is discussed in the first paragraph of the English version on this page?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The first paragraph discusses criminal activity conducted on the territory of SBWS as well as Vojvodina by a number of people who are identified as registered criminals and smugglers and who, according to the document, have call it links or connections with leaders of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, and then the names of these people are given, as well as officials in the government of the RSK, SBWS, and UNPROFOR and the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please read out the names of the individuals who are identified in the sentence, "They are closely connected with top leaders of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The names are Stanisic, Loncarevic, Prica, and Kostic, Radoslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And respect to the government of the RSK in the Serbian region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, could you please identify those individuals that are contained in this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Goran Hadzic, who was at the time the president of the RSK; Ilija Kojic, then last names are given, Zivanovic, Radlovic, Spanovic, and Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the lower portion of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the footnote on this page does it identify who the registered criminals are that are being refer to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, I mean, a number of names are given there, Arkan, the Dimitrije brothers, Zika Ivanovic, and then yeah, additional names are given.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What are the additional names?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: A Bozovic and a Loginov.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And what does this footnote continue to state about those individuals?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The footnote states that they have SDB State Security Service membership cards and that they go to the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, please go ahead and continue explaining the footnote.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Okay. There's also a reference to an aka Cope, who is owner of a few private companies in Belgrade. I mean that's -- I think this refers again to the criminals or the term "criminals." There's aka Frenki, aka Carli, Lainovic Branko and Ranko who are smuggling drugs and goods from it says there Western Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this footnote it mentions Zika Ivanovic. Based on your analysis in this case do you know who this individual is and what other names he is known by?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I have seen, I mean, Zivojin Ivanovic, and he was mentioned in connections to units identified as special -- unit -- a unit, excuse me, as a Special Purpose Unit of the MUP of Serbia and that was also -- I mean, his name was then -- not an aka, it was -- or an aka was Crnogorac which means Montenegrin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1075 marked for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I perhaps seek first some clarification. Apparently what we see in the footnote, Mr. Theunens, is the listing of the criminals. Is that, I have to understand it, Arkan, the Dimitrije brothers, all closely related to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, because if we would move back to the top of the page we see that this asterisk or the star --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- is put there after the word criminal so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- they are specified in the footnote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I find in the footnote the name of Loginov and Loginov further in the text is referred to as someone in the UNPROFOR as apparently a person with whom the criminals had close contact. Is that -- now, I find him both on the list of the criminals and on the -- apparently the important persons these criminals had links to. That confuses me, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could we go in closed session, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can go into closed session. We move into closed session, and you explain in closed session why we have to be in closed session. Private session will do, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or private, yeah. Something that is not public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least the content. They will still see you. One second. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, it would be our position that that could be and should be evidence that's in a public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The evidence as we have heard it until now -- perhaps not to discuss this in open session, Mr. Jordash. That's -- because it then goes to the details. Let me -- let's return for a second into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Continue. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the Prosecution please have P1075 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this exhibit is referenced in parts 1, 2, and 3 of your report and discussed on pages 101 and 102 of part 1. The e-court page is page 124 and 125. Directing your attention to the first few lines of this document, are you able to determine which security organ was the originator of this report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was my -- my conclusion that this document had been compiled by a member of the security organs of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the subject of this report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The subject is -- it's a report on the formation of the JCO, a special operations unit of the RDB, republican state security of Serbia, and interesting data for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 9 of the English version and page 6 of the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you able to determine the approximate date of this report based on its contents?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes. We can see in title 5 that reference is made to an event that took place on the 4th and the 13th of May, 1996, which means that the report has to date from after the 13th of May, 1996. I think there's also another reference in the document to May 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is discussed in section 5 of this report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It discusses an award ceremony by people or members -- no. Sorry. People receive awards from the Ministry of Interior and the Republic of Serbia state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this report indicate whether or not there is a laying of any wreath?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. In the second and the third line following title 5, there is reference to a wreath which is laid in the centre in Kula at the monument of Mr. Radoslav Kostic, and he is then identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 10 of the English translation and remain on the same page of the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this page indicate anyone who were award recipients at this ceremony?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes. A number of names are given, Milorad Ulemek also known as Legija, who is then described as Arkan's general; Predrag Baklajic, also known as Baklaja, who is identified as the head of a terrorist group in Kordun, and apparently he has been liquidated. And then also a Milan Letica who has, according to the document, also been liquidated in a mutual showdown in Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of the English translation of this document and page 2 of the B/C/S version shown to the witness. If we could please have the bottom half of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is discussed in section 2 of this report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Section 2 discusses as the title states paramilitary units and groups and their connection with the special units of the republican state security and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What does this section say about those groups?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It identifies a number of these groups and then discusses in general terms their activities in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, i.e., the territory of the RSK and RS during which -- I mean during these activities according to the document they remained in direct contact with the republican state security and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Which groups are identified?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It starts off with the SDG, so the Serbian Volunteer Guard, under Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, and then the special unit of the Ministry of Interior which is under the command of someone who is described as the self-appointed Colonel Vasilije Mijovic, the Red Berets, and then a special under the command of Zika Ivanovic, also known as Crnogorac, excuse me, Crnogorac, and then a unit described as the paramilitary unit of Slobodan Medic, also known as Boca.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on your review of materials in this case, were any of these units ever brought together for any combat operations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I don't have an exact recollection that they were all present at the same time in one particular location, but for example -- I mean, one good example which I've discussed in my report is the Pauk command which is established in the course of November 1994 in Western Bosnia Herzegovina. There we see that a number of these individuals and the corresponding groups operate together under a -- a Joint Command in a co-ordinated manner with units of the VRS and the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has completed its examination of part 1 of the Theunens report, and at this time the Prosecution would tender exhibits from this part. We are able to go through these in certain ranges if it's easier for the Chamber to facilitate the tendering. The exhibits being tendered are those to which there is no objection by either the Stanisic or the Simatovic Defence. The Prosecution tenders Exhibits P1010 to P1047, and we request that P1046 and P1047 remain under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does this -- the numbers reflect the documents which are not opposed to. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I make a mistake, P1010, up to and including P1047 are admitted into evidence. P1046 and P1047 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders P1051 to 1052, P1054 to P1057 requesting that Exhibit P1051 remain under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again looking at the Defence, apparently no objections. P1051, P1052, P1054, P1055, P1056, and P1057 are admitted into evidence. P1051 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders P1062 to P1064, P1066, P1074, and P1076 to P1079, and we request that Exhibits P1062, P1064, and P1076 to P1079 remain under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1062 up to and including P1064 are admitted into evidence, the first and the last under seal. P1063 as a public document. P1066, P1074 are admitted into evidence. P1076 up to and including P1079 are admitted into evidence, all four under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm a bit. There is some confusion, Mr. Weber. I think I heard you say, that's at least what we find on the record, P1054 to P1057, which would include P1055, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this resolves confusion between the Chamber and registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have I dealt with everything, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There is one last segment of exhibits from part 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's P1081 to P1082, P1086 to P1089, and Exhibit P1091. We are requesting that -- and all those can be admitted as public exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. P1081, P1082, P1086 up to and including P1089 and P1091 are admitted as public documents. Then later I take it that we get a list of the documents which should -- are not tendered yet and which will -- there will be further submissions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in part 2 of your report you discuss the contextual developments throughout the conflict in Croatia. Today the Prosecution will first focus on particular developments and aspects of the conflict in the Serb Autonomous Region of the Krajina and then the SAO SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1101, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: While the exhibit's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, one short remark. The last document we had on our screen on which you asked questions has bit of an odd way of translating. Sometimes abbreviations such as SRK are translated by SRK. Sometimes when you find in the original MUP you'll find not an abbreviation in the translation but -- or RDB is not transposed as RDB and then with an explanation but just gives the full explanation of the text, and it's the way in which that document is translated is not very consistent, and I would like you to have a look at those inconsistencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for mentioning that and I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Prior to the commencement of hostilities, were there any changes in the structure of the police and the Territorial Defence in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as a very general conclusion, one can say that starting in the spring 1991, local Serbs start to set up their own structures, own police and/or Territorial Defence structures in areas where they have a significant presence. In some areas they do it themselves. In other areas they remove the Croats or -- in -- in other areas the Croats abandon the existing structures themselves. And there are examples listed in the document -- in the report, I'm sorry, to explain how this affects the creation of a local Serb TO in an area which became known as the SAO Krajina, as well as the SAO SBWS and the SAO Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Turning your attention to the exhibit that is now before you which is discussed on page 22 of part 2, e-court page 165, could you please tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: This document is -- is a -- I mean, as the title says, an order issued by Dr. Milan Babic, who is the President of the Executive Board of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina. This is at the very early stages. It's from April -- the 1st of April, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under the conclusion, are there any requests that are contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Milan Babic requests the government of the Republic of Serbia that forces of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia provide technical and personnel support to the secretariat of interior of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On this same day, that being the 1st of April, 1991, were there any other decisions issued by the SAO Krajina Executive Council?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I think further on in my report -- I thought I put a note here, but there's also a decision to include the Serb autonomous region of Krajina into the Republic of Serbia, and I'm trying to -- yeah. It's on page 26 basically. It's P1107. Page 26 of part 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P426 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This exhibit is referenced on page 65 of part 2 of your report, which is e-court page 208. Mr. Theunens, this is a proposal to set up a new training centre, dated 27 May 1991. Who is this proposal from?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: We would have to go to the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have the next page briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's -- as we can see it at the bottom it's sent by Captain Dragan Vasiljkovic to a number of addressees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: While we are on this page, could you please tell us who the addressees on this document are.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: They're not -- I mean, they are titles, but the names of the persons are not given, so it's the president of the Municipal Assembly, which would most likely be the Municipal Assembly in Knin. The secretary of the SUP, which would most likely be Mr. Milan Martic. The security service. It's -- I know that there was a -- a kind of a -- of a State Security Service in the Krajina at the time, but it was not fully organised. So it's not -- not possible for me to be more precise there. And then the commander of the Territorial Defence, which at least according to the document should have been Milan Babic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please return to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does Captain Dragan discuss any special units of the SAO Krajina in this proposal?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, he does, in the -- in the second paragraph on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have the lower portion of the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the proposal?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It's twofold. I mean, Dragan proposes how the unit should be composed. I mean, active and activated or reserve members. And he also gives a number of tasks in relation here more specifically the training centre and the fortress.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this proposal, where would the training of these special units take place?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It would take place in Golubic, which is near Knin Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1117 in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the next exhibit is a decision to form Special Purpose Police Units of the SAO Krajina dated 29 May 1991. According to this decision, which is now appearing before you. Who had authority over these newly formed Special Purpose Units of the SAO Krajina MUP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: As you said in the third line under decision they would be under the authority of the Ministry of Defence, and I've highlighted that in my report. It coincides with the appointment of Milan Martic, who was already secretary of the interior. Here now he's appointed minister of defence on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is this decision on the election of Milan Martic as the minister of defence, dated 29 May 1991, if you can confirm if that's P1116, marked for identification. I believe this is on page 33.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah. P1116. Yeah, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did Milan Martic maintain any other positions throughout 1991 besides the one listed on this document, or in P1116?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, he was -- as I mentioned, he was first secretary of internal affairs and then because the names were changed, this happened also in Serbia, after he was elected secretary of internal affairs, which is P1119, on the 27th of June, 1991, he was -- I put it as re-elected minister of interior of the SAO Krajina, and that is P1118. And this is discussed on page 34 of part 2 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1179 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the exhibit that is being brought up before you is discussed on pages 67 and 68 of part 2 of your report. This is e-court page 210 to 211. Could you please tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: This is a note, and I think on the bottom it will be marked -- it is marked that it was sent by -- or compiled by Dragan Vasiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
