utterances.text: Are you able to determine the approximate date of this note based on its contents and your review of other documents referenced in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah. On this page one can see under the third line says, "I suggest," and then there is a heading 1. Dragan uses the future tense for the date of the 23rd of June, which would mean that it has been compiled prior to the 23rd of June, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on the content of this note, did you reach any conclusions as to which state security department it was sent to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I looked at this document in the context of the other documents, and some of them we have discussed this afternoon, and my conclusion is that this document is sent to the state security of the Republic of Serbia. And again also looking at the contents where he talks about, for example, Milan Martic, Frenki, I considered it again in the context of the other documents unlikely that he would address Milan Martic -- or address, I mean -- discuss Milan Martic in a document sent to the state security of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What does Captain Dragan suggest as a programme for further training for special units on this page?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah. He makes a suggestion -- I mean, I can read it out if you want, but he makes a suggestion on how the structures -- I mean the instructors should be used. He also, I mean further on, suggests that he, Milan Martic and Frenki and what he describes as influential Specials should give advice to the units in the field about -- in relation to future development -- further development. Yeah, I mean I discuss it on page 67 in my report. So I'm just referring to that now if there's anything I want to add. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1186, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the Prosecution will now show you three exhibits and then ask you about what these documents demonstrate. The first exhibit which is now before you is Exhibit P1186. It is a 19 July 1991 report from Glina which is discussed on page 70 of part 2, which is e-court page 213. Could you please tell us what information is contained in this report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Dragan provides an overview of the -- of the current situation in Glina where he gives an overview of the incidents and other events that have happened in the previous days -- or in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the bottom of the original document which is on the top of the English translation, could you please tell us who is on the addressee list of this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Dragan has -- or included five addressees. The first is the secretary of the SUP of the SAO Krajina which -- who is -- I mean which is Milan Martic. The commander -- the second is the commander of the SAO Krajina TO, which would be Milan Babic. The second -- the third, I'm sorry, third is identified as Frenki, then fourth we have Major Fica, Fica, I'm sorry, and then there is a security officer. Now, it's not clear what he means by "security officer." And, okay, the Major Fica in my conclusion is the same -- is the Fico we saw earlier in the SSNO security organs document from August 1991, Dragan Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P1121, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Exhibit P1121 is a report of the SAO Krajina TO staff, dated 19 July 1991. It is referenced on page 71 of part 2 of your report, e-court page 214. Could you please tell us who are the addressees on this report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It starts with the president of the council of the People's Committee of the SAO Krajina. I have to confess that I didn't look into detail into that title. It's my understanding that this is Milan Babic. Then there's the secretary of the SUP for the SAO Krajina, aka Milan Martic. ODB could stand for Odoljenje [phoen] DB, or DBTBs and the state security. The commander of the TO SAO Krajina, which was also Milan Babic at the time because there was no staff yet, military staff for the TO of the SAO Krajina. And then Frenki.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1122, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Theunens, you said ODB could stand for. Does it stand for, and if it stands for DB, is that state security, and what stands the O for? We have no -- because in the translation we see that the abbreviation is unknown to the translator, and I would like to abuse your presence or perhaps the parties could even agree on what ODB exactly stands for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm not sure whether I was confused, whether we still have the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. We have a different document now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But it explains --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the abbreviation, one of the -- was the ODB. Now -- oh, here we have -- yes. Yes, because here apparently the interpreter knows what ODB stands for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. It's a pity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: State security department.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It should have clarified that before, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in the previous document the ODB is apparently an unknown abbreviation which surprised me a bit, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If it assists, we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everyone agrees. Yes. So it not only could stand for but it does stand for. Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the document that now appears before you? The Prosecution brought it up as P1122.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Okay. It's another -- it's a situation report. I mean, you can see at the bottom of the screen situation report covering the situation 5, 6 of August 1991, compiled by -- okay, a body known as the SAO Krajina TO staff, but again I explained in my report a military commander is only appointed in September, and this is dated the 6th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who is on the addressee list for this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The term Supreme Commander SAO Krajina TO is used, who is Milan Babic. The secretary of the SAO Krajina SUP, Milan Martic. The ODB, as discussed. The commander of the TO where I'm not able to -- to identify him because I'm not sure at which level we're talking. And then Frenki.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. What do the last three exhibits demonstrate about the reporting system that may have existed between the individuals listed on these reports?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Well, the documents show that attempts are made to establish and to have a reporting system function and that the reports are sent to a number of people. And as I mentioned earlier in the reports, such reports are sent on a need-to-know basis, i.e., they are sent to people who have a need to know the information in order to prepare their decision making and planning and that -- okay, Milan Babic, Milan Martic, as well as Frenki are among these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What co-ordination if any, do these documents illustrate?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It's difficult to answer. I mean, the question, it shows -- the documents showed that, I assume you're referring to Frenki, that Frenki has a need to know what is happening in the Krajina, what the units of the SAO Krajina are doing, and over a longer time period. I mean, we have seen documents covering different time periods.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On pages 24 and 25 of part 2, this is e-court page -- pages 167 and 168, you discuss Exhibit P1105, a decision to apply the law of defence of the Republic of Serbia on the territory of the SAO Krajina. Pursuant to Article 5 of this decision, what units officially constituted the armed forces of the SAO Krajina as of the 1st of August, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The armed forces of the SAO Krajina as explained in Article 5 of P1105 consists of the SAO Krajina Territorial Defence and the Special Purpose Units of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 45 of part 2 of your report, e-court page 188, you state the following opinion: "In many parts of the combat zone in Croatia, the JNA established operational OG and tactical groups and in some areas also assault detachments JOD and assault groups to create the conditions for or restore and maintain (and unified) command over all forces involved in combat operations." My question to you is what do you mean by the word "restore" in this opinion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I mean by this that single authority is one of the three principles of command and control in the SFRY Armed Forces. Now, since in an earlier question you asked -- we see that local -- the local Serbs or the Serbs in Krajina as well as Western Slavonia and SBWS established their own structures. This doesn't happen everywhere as smooth as it was maybe intended to happen, and so it means that -- I mean, the implications are there are different groups existing at different times, and since we are -- or there are combat operations ongoing and they are intensifying after summer 1991, there is a need to bring all these units which may not have existed before, to bring all these units under single command or single authority. Yeah, single command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution does not have a substantial number of further questions for you today regarding the events in the SAO SBWS. The Prosecution's next questions will mainly relate to your analysis of the relationship between Arkan and the SDG to the JNA in this region. According to the materials referenced in your report, are there indications that Arkan and the SDG were subordinated to operational groups of the JNA during combat operations in the region of the SBWS.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: In my report I explain that the JNA was organised in two operational groups during the combat in Slavonia, Baranja -- yeah, Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. There was an Operation Group North and an Operational Group South with the Vuka River which cuts Vukovar into being the -- the boundary between the two operational groups, and Arkan during combat operations acted under the command of Operational Group North. I don't have any specific documents on his subordination during combat operations led by OG North, but I have a reference in the second part of my report on page 94 to a speech, the command of Operational Group North General Andrija Biorcevic made in January 1992 where he -- I mean the wording he uses indicates subordination of Arkan to OG North-led combat operations at the time. The other documents I discuss in my reports -- report, and these are mainly reports by security organs of the 1st Military District, indicate that there is -- that Arkan is doing a number of things without being subordinated to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P327 in evidence. The Prosecution requests that this document not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I notice that one of the -- one of the previous documents bears the stamps of under what number they are admitted in other case, and that's something we try to avoid, as you may be aware of. So therefore, if a better copy could be uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that also. And just so it's on the record, it's Exhibit P1122 and we will look into that over the next recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because otherwise it leads to all kinds of confusion, at least that's a risk. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 89 of part 2 of your report you reference this exhibit. It's e-court page 232. Could you please identify this exhibit and tell us the subject of the report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: This is a report compiled by a security organ of a logistic sector. It's not specified but it should be logistic sector or the logistic centre of the 1st Military District of the JNA, and it's information on Zeljko Raznjatovic, also known as Arkan, with a number of observations which they then send to the security administration OB, so at the level of the SSNO, security which is also at the SSNO, and indeed -- that's it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the Prosecution's question to you relates to the top paragraph. How does this report describe Arkan's relationship with the 51st Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: According to the report, Arkan behaves cynically and tyrannically towards the members of the 51st Motorised Brigade, whereby he actually also kicked two officers of that brigade out of the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, continuing to the next paragraph, does this report describe any independent actions taken by Arkan and his group?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It does. It has to be -- I mean, just to provide some context, by the 1st of October large parts of the AO, the area of responsibility, sorry, of OG North are fully under JNA control. There is no more fighting, so there are no more combat operations. And as this document indicates, Arkan and his group are active there independently and doing certain things. As is explained here they are visiting Croatian houses, interrogating the inhabitants there, and according to the document, they are committing crimes against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could please have the lower half of the English translation. In the second paragraph from the bottom of the translation, does this report indicate who the JNA members think is supporting Arkan?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, according to the document JNA members think that Arkan is doing what he's doing, or as described in the document, with the full support of the SDB, the State Security Service of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this completes the Prosecution's examination of part 2 of the report. Whatever Your Honours would like me to do. I can continue and tender all the exhibits from this, or if you would just like me to go through one larger tendering process after part 3, I could continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could do it all together. If you would prepare it in a little note, then you could just follow so that we don't have to do it twice, your reading it first and then me reading it again. So if you would -- and then show it to the Defence first to see whether they agree with the list and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I am looking at the clock. Perhaps this would also be a suitable moment for having a break, and we will resume at 10 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move for a moment into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution's examination today on part 3 of your report will focus on the presence of particular individuals and aspects of events that occurred in five specific municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1381, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, while the exhibit is being called up, on pages 55 to 54 of part 3 of your report, e-court pages 336 to 355, you discuss events which occurred in the municipality of Zvornik. The Prosecution will show you three exhibits in relation to this municipality. Directing your attention to the exhibit now before you, which is discussed on page 58 of part 3, e-court page 339, could you please tell us what this exhibit is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a situation report compiled by the command of the 17th corps, i.e., the JNA unit at the time in north-eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina, discussing the situation in its zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have paragraph 3 focused upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 3 does this report provide any description of the situation in Zvornik as of the 6th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. At the end of the paragraph it states that the situation in Zvornik municipality is "explosive and likely to grow into a large conflict, because Serb and Muslim TO were mobilised."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of both English and B/C/S of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to paragraph 5 of the situation report. Does this report describe the command and deployment of JNA units in the zone of responsibility of the 17th JNA Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed. I mean, we also have the commander, the name of the commander, Major-General Savo Jankovic. He explains to the addressee, which should be the 2nd Military District, what his units are doing and where they are -- I mean, he explains that units are primarily deployed to secure military facilities, control the territory, prevent -- and prevent conflicts as well as, yeah, further issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1380, marked for identification. It is a cable to General Jankovic, dated 8 April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you could, please tell us what is communicated to General Jankovic in this cable?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It's the director of the state-owned or the public construction company Izet Mehinagic. He communicates his concern about the situation in Zvornik, including what he describes as the issuance of an ultimatum, and he wants General Savo Jankovic to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are any negotiations discussed in this cable?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, he talks about negotiations in Mali Zvornik which is located on the Serbian side of the border where according to Mehinagic Arkan is the chief negotiator which representatives of the Zvornik -- I mean Bosnia-Herzegovina municipality. He also mentions the attendance of a Captain Dragan Obrenovic who is a JNA officer, and then three other people, an Alija, an Abdulah, and a Jovo Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P1390, marked for identification. It is 2nd Military District JNA situation report, dated 10 April 1992. Your Honour, if I could just please have a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In section 3 of this document entitled "Situation in the Territory," does this report describe the situation in the Zvornik municipality as of the 10th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It does. I mean, the 2nd Military District covers the largest part of Bosnia-Herzegovina except for a small part in eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina, and so the situation in a number of municipalities all over Bosnia-Herzegovina as -- including Zvornik is discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And how does it describe the situation as of the 10th of April, 1992, and does it communicate any concerns?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It states that the situation is getting more intensified, specifically in the areas of Visegrad, Zvornik, as well as Jajce and Sarajevo, and then he talks also about the attitude of the population towards the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the English and B/C/S of this document. And if we could particularly have the section that is entitled "17K."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you please tell us if this report describes the deployment of JNA forces in and around Zvornik as of the 10th of April, 1992, under the section that starts with 17K?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed. Now we're in the activities of the subordinate units of the 2nd Military District, and this is the 17th corps, and it mentions that the units are fully engaged in arranging the preparation of mobilisation. They are securing traffic on the main roads and they are monitoring the situation in the crisis points or crisis areas in the zone of responsibility. And then he provides details on the situation in Zvornik and Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What are the details in relation to the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: According to the document, Serb paramilitary formations are holding about 3.000 Muslims under ultimatum in the Kula area. And in the afternoon, 20 buses without Muslims -- Muslim paramilitary soldiers proceeded from Tuzla to Zvornik. I mean, that's all for -- for Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on the last three exhibits, how would you describe the level of engagement of JNA forces between the 6th and the 10th of April, 1992, in and around the Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we know from -- from the other documents that between 8 and 9 April or during 8 and 9 April Serb forces take control of Zvornik, and these forces are specified in my report, and based on the report of the 17th corps, the 17th corps is not actively participating in this takeover. They are focusing, as we saw in the previous report, on protecting military facilities, they're manning or they're securing traffic on the main roads, and they are monitoring the situation but they -- at least on the basis of these documents and other documents I reviewed, they're not actively involved in the takeover the control of the municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I know this is in your report, but since you've mention it, who are the Serb forces that are involved in the takeover of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I discussed that in the section on Zvornik. There are members of the Territorial Defence of Loznica, which is a municipality in Serbia. There are -- I mean, according to these JNA documents we saw Arkan is involved, and there's also a paramilitary group which became known as the Yellow Wasps involved. And then there is information provided by Vojislav Seselj that also members of the Special Purpose Unit of the ministry of the interior of the Republic of Serbia is involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on your analysis, was there any subordination of Arkan and the SDG to the JNA between the 6th and the 10th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I mean, as far as Zvornik is concerned, I haven't seen any documents that would suggest that. Again, as I mentioned, the documents I've seen indicate that JNA units in the area adopted a passive [Realtime transcript read in error "positive"] posture and were not actively involved in the takeover.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On pages 74 to 79 of part 3 of your report, you discuss events which occurred in the municipality of Bosanski Samac. This is on e-court pages 355 to 370. In this section, you discuss an individual by the name of Dragan Djordjevic, also known as Crni. Could you please tell us if Crni participated in combat operations --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to get to my feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I heard a word before posture at, Your Honours, line 5, and I didn't hear that word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed. I'm sorry I forgot to check the transcript. It should be they didn't adopt -- they adopted a passive posture, not a positive posture. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which brings me to another matter. Your answer was focusing on the attitude of this JNA rather than on what was the question, whether there was only subordination. I can keep my own troops quiet and passive, and at the same time have some other units subordinated and doing the takeovers. So I had some difficulties in finding the direct answer to the question that was put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise for that, Your Honours. I -- as I tried to explain, I haven't seen any documents indicating that Arkan during the takeover of Zvornik was subordinated to the JNA. And actually, the reason why I refer to JNA was that the documents I have seen do not indicate any JNA involvement either in the takeover. That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it was a double answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't see any subordination in documents and also no active involvement of the JNA. Now, SDG was part of the question as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Arkan SDG stands for the Serbian Volunteer Guard which is another name for Arkan's unit. So the same applies. I have not seen any document indicating a subordination of the SDG to the JNA during the takeover of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Returning to my question about Bosanski Samac. As I indicated, you discuss an individual by the name of Dragan Djordjevic in this section. Could you please tell us if Dragan Djordjevic, also known as Crni, participated in combat operations in and around the municipality of Bosanski Samac between April and June 1992.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Dragan Djordjevic, also known as Crni, was commander of a detachment or a group of military personnel which was subordinated to the JNA-led Tactical Group 17 during the takeover of Bosanski Samac and as such participated in the takeover.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on your analysis, what relationship did Crni have with the MUP of Serbia in 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I discussed that on page 78 of part 3 of the report. According to statements Crni or Dragan Djordjevic made himself, he was an official of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is there any information that you reviewed as to where Crni had trained during the course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, I've included information according to which he was an instructor at the Pajzos training facility in Eastern Slavonia, which was as other documents in my report indicate was used by members of the Special Purpose Unit of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia to train volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On pages 99 to 107 of part 3 of your report, you discuss events which occurred in the municipality of Doboj in 1992. This is e-court pages 380 to 388. In this section, you discuss an individual by the name of Raja Bozovic. What could you determine about the relationship between Raja Bozovic and the MUP of Serbia based on your review of documents?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Raja Bozovic, the name appears several times when discussing -- I mean, events I discuss in the report. And in addition to the documents that I've included in the Doboj section where link -- link is established between Bozovic and Red Berets or unit identified as Red Berets, we also know that he was a commander of a subordinate unit, a tactical group, I'm not sure Tactical Group 2 or Tactical Group 3, in the Pauk command which was active in western Bosnia-Herzegovina between November 1994 and August 1995. And as - just to answer the question - as is discussed in the report, Pauk was predominantly manned by members of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia, including members of the Special Purpose Unit. There is also information indicating that he was involved in Skelani, as again in charge of a Red Beret unit, and this is P1441 and P399 that indicate that. And this refers to 1992 -- end of 1992, early 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P1452 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: While the next exhibit's being called up, on pages 120 to 129 of part 3 of your report, you discuss events which occurred in and around Trnovo during June and July 1995. These are e-court pages 401 to 410. Directing your attention to the RS MUP dispatch dated 1 July 1995 that now before you, does this exhibit refer to any units of the Serbian MUP who participated in combat operations near Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it does. It talks about a Kajman Detachment which consists -- or which includes two platoons, more specifically the Plavi and the Skopje platoon, and the Kajman Detachment is identified as a unit of MUP Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to this report, does it indicate whether or not any members of the Serbian MUP forces were injured during combat operations? Please let us know if you need us to read on -- or scroll down?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, if we could scroll down. Yes. Sorry -- eight lines from the bottom there is a reference to yesterday's fighting or clashes, and during those clashes three members of the MUP Serbia were lightly wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And when did this fighting take place?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: This should have -- I mean, taking into account the date of the report, which is the 1st of July, it should have been on the 30th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1454, marked for identification. It is a 1 July 1995 response from General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what is the subject of this response from General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: General Mladic responds to a telegram of the anti-terrorist unit of the MUP Serbia from the day -- the day before, and he deals with the evacuation -- or the use, excuse me, the use of helicopters from the VRS for the evacuation of members of MUP Serbia who are participating in the fighting in the Trnovo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to the -- this response, does General Mladic authorise this use?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed. And -- and -- I mean, from the contextual point of view, this is an important document to highlight the level of co-ordination that is required to organise the involvement of call it nonorganic, i.e., non-VRS forces, in this case MUP Serbia forces in joint operations with the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where is the basis of that opinion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Well, the basis -- sorry. The basis of that opinion is that it requires the authorisation of the chief of the VRS Main Staff in order to allow injured members, I mean in this specific matter, injured members of the MUP Serbia units fighting in -- participating in the fighting in Trnovo to make use of a VRS helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How does this response indicate officials from the MUP of Serbia should be notified?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Well, General Mladic states that the MUP of the RS should inform I mean representatives of the MUP Serbia, and then a Colonel Golic of his decision pertaining to the use of the helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1469, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 128 of part 3 of your report, e-court page 409, you reference this dispatch dated 22 July 1995. What does this document indicate as to who the Skorpion Unit belongs to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: More or less in the middle of the document we can see that -- I would say ten page -- ten lines from the top that the Skorpions are identified as a unit of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What activities are the Skorpions engaged in according to this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The Skorpions are holding a defence line.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this dispatch indicate when the forces of the MUP Serbia would be leaving the battlefront of Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes. Four lines lower, it stated that the units -- or the MUP of Serbia forces will be leaving on the 22nd and the 23rd of July, and this is highlighted by the commander as -- as a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of Exhibit P289 in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On pages 130 to 134 of part 3 of your report, you discuss events which occurred in Sanski Most in September 1995. This is e-court pages 411 to 415.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could also please have the page 2 of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is a dispatch dated 23 September 1995 from General Mladic. Does the first paragraph of this exhibit indicate whether Arkan and his SDG formations are under the command of the VRS up until the 23rd of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It indicates that they are -- these SDG formations are present in the area of responsibility of the 1st Battalion or the 1st Brigade of the 2nd Krajina Corps, but according to Mladic they are not subordinated to the VRS, and he explains the basis for his conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the basis that he explains?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Okay. They haven't -- they have not taken part in any combat operations. They are not part of any formation unit, and they have not reported, i.e., presented themselves to any of the commands, battalion-level commands, of the VRS, and they haven't, yeah, present themselves to the Main Staff of the VRS either. So they haven't received any assignments from the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the middle paragraph on this page. Does this exhibit indicate how VRS members are being recruited into the SDG and how their salaries and benefits would be paid if they joined?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed. That is explained in -- in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What does it say?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It says in the third paragraph that they are being promised money, 600 dinars, 10.000 dinars -- excuse me. They are presented a salary of 600 dinars and a compensation of 10.000 dinars in case they are -- get wounded, as well as unemployment and health insurance through the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia. That is what members of the SDG promised to this -- to people they tried to recruit from the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does the following paragraph describe any crimes being committed by the SDG in and around Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, it does. I mean, mention is made of liquidation of a certain number of what are described as loyal Muslim citizens, including relatives of a VRS serviceman. And, okay, there's justification given.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of the English version of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under number 2, does General Mladic in this dispatch make any proposals to the organs of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah. He requests and proposes that the organs of the MUP take measures within their jurisdiction against Raznjatovic and his formations for the crimes they have committed against VRS members and civilians, and he much bases that on the fact that Arkan has identified himself as a member of the MUP of Serbia and MUP of VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time this completes the Prosecution's examination-in-chief of Mr. Theunens. We did provide a list of documents -- or list of exhibits that are not being opposed by either Defence teams, and at this time we would ask to tender those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have received a list. Have the Defence teams received that same list, documents for which admission is sought?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it reflects that these are the documents not objected to by the Defence; is that correct? I'm also looking at you, Mr. Bakrac. Apparently it is. Then I'll try to go through it rather quickly, and I -- P1092 and P1093 are admitted into evidence. P1095, up to and including P1158 are admitted into evidence. Among these, P1096 and P1131 are admitted under seal, the others as public documents. P1161, P1162 both admitted into evidence. P1165 up to and including P1173 are admitted into evidence. 1165 to 1167, 1169, 1170, and 1172 under seal. P1175 up to and including P1176 are admitted into evidence. P1180, P1182, P1183, P1184, and P1185 are admitted into evidence. P1187 up to and including P1191 are admitted into evidence. P1188 under seal. P1195 up to and including P1208 are admitted into evidence. P1200 under seal. P1211 to P1216, and I said to, including also P1216, are admitted into evidence. P1218 and P1219 are admitted into evidence. P1221 to P1247, including that last number, are admitted into evidence. P1249 up to and including P1281 are admitted into evidence. Among them, P1254 and P1260 admitted under seal. P1283 up to and including P1284 are admitted into evidence. P1286 up it and including P1301, as well as P1303 are admitted into evidence. I now move to the documents related to part 3. P1306 up to and including P1338 are admitted into evidence. Among them, P1319 under seal. P1340 to P1343 are admitted into evidence. P1347 up to and including P1367 are admitted. Among them, P1346, P1347, and P1349 under seal. P1369 up to and including P1373 are admitted into evidence. P1378 up to and including P1381 are admitted into evidence. P1383 up to and including P1395 are admitted into evidence. P1389 under seal. P1397 to P1398 are admitted. P1403 up to and including P1411 are admitted into evidence. P1413 up to and including P1421 are admitted into evidence. However, P1417 under seal. P1423 is admitted. P1425 to P1434, the last number included, are admitted. P1427 under seal. P1436 up to and including P1437, P1440 [Realtime transcript read in error "P1444"] up to and including P1442 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt you. Was it P1440?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was P1440, yes, yes, because otherwise we would count back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, I believe the transcript on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it says P1444. And it was meant to be one sentence, which means that 1436 and 1437 are included in the admission. Then followed by P1440 up to and including P1442. The next series: P1444 up to and including P1449 are admitted into evidence. P1444 and P1445 under seal. P1451 and P1452 are admitted, as well as P1454 up to and including P1479. First of all, I would like to thank you for your patience for listening to this reciting of a list, but I hope everyone has carefully checked that we have the right numbers now in evidence. Thank you, Mr. Weber. Who is the first to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Jordash, it will be you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Good afternoon Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In the little time that we have left today, I would like to just try to understand before we launch into the body of the report the precise conclusions that you reached concerning the relationship of the Serbian MUP to the paramilitaries. You effectively divide the relationship into two types. Is this right? On the one hand, Arkan, Captain Dragan, and the Red Berets were controlled by the Serbian MUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: That is not correct. I mean, it doesn't reflect what I tried to write in the report. When I first address volunteers/paramilitary groups controlled to -- controlled by, I'm sorry, or related otherwise to the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia, I start off with Dragan and the people he operated with. Secondly, I talk about Arkan; and thirdly, I talk about other groups whereby these other groups are then further defined. As I mentioned earlier, the material that was available to me did not allow to draw a -- what I say a complete conclusion as to what was the exact nature of the relations between the various groups and the Ministry of Interior. I mean, the documents I have included in particular when I discussed the involvement of these groups, and I'm talking now about all of them, Dragan, Arkan, as well as the other groups, for what -- their involvement in the conflict in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina is concerned show a number of things that allowed -- led me conclude that there was a degree of control, i.e., influence over the activities of these various units.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I ask you, please, to turn to the executive summary of the report, page 6, and it's paragraph 9, e-court page 6. And at paragraph 9 -- sorry. Exhibit P1575, MFI'd. Because -- perhaps it's my reading, Mr. Theunens, but it seemed that in the report you were a little more definite in the way that you looked at the paramilitaries. At page 9 -- sorry, page 6, paragraph 9: "The SFRY Supreme Command, the JNA, and the government of the Republic of Serbia, in particular the ministry of interior and ministry of defence, were aware of the existence of extra-legal voluntary -- volunteer/paramilitary formations participating in the conflict in Croatia as well as the role of Serbian nationalistic political parties in the recruitment of these volunteers and encouraged these groups or supported them otherwise." And then you move on -- if we of move to the next page, page 7 in e-court, to paragraph 10, you note: "At the same time, there were also volunteer/paramilitary groups such as Arkan's Tigers ... and individuals operating under the command of Dragan or other groups including a group which became colloquially known as the Red Berets which were controlled by the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia, the latter through Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic, aka Frenki." Are you not making a distinction here? And you're saying, well, there are on the one hand there is the groups which were formed by nationalistic parties, and on the other hand there's Arkan's, there's Captain Dragan's and the Red Berets, and I am asserting that the Red Berets were in fact controlled directly by Stanisic and Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: That is correct, and I apologise if I misunderstood your initial question but I didn't see any reference to the nationalistic political parties in your initial question. I understood from your initial question that you believed that I had made a distinction within -- I mean between Arkan, Dragan, and others within the Ministry of the Interior. So I mean I stand by what I wrote in my report because the misunderstanding's clarified now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So just so that I'm clear, you're -- you effectively concluded that there were on the one hand paramilitary groups created by the political parties such as the White Eagles - and we'll come to the list in a moment - they were, is this correct, tacitly authorised by the government of the Serbia, including the Serbian MUP. On the other hand, Arkan's Men, Captain Dragan's men, and the Red Berets were controlled by the Serbian MUP with direct control of the Red Berets by Stanisic and Simatovic. Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I didn't include the word "direct," but otherwise, I mean that's a fair summary. I mean, we can talk about control. I didn't use the word "direct" in -- in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But you did make the distinction between Dragan and Arkan on the one side and the Red Berets on the other, attaching Simatovic and Stanisic to the Red Berets with a more intimate relationship than that to Arkan or to Captain Dragan. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I -- I don't think I did that. I mean, I didn't have the material that would allow me to do so. My conclusion was that all three of them -- I mean, if you say Arkan, Dragan, the Red Berets, they were all controlled -- and again the word "control" has to be taken in its --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We'll come to the word control in a minute.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But you do say, sorry to interrupt --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- but you do say the latter through Stanisic and Simatovic as if -- and doesn't the latter relate to Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Okay. Now I understand, I'm sorry. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you do in the executive summary at least make a distinction; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: No, that's true. That's correct, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you had in mind --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I wasn't concentrate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- in terms of the two accused that their relationship to the Red Berets was closer than it was to or Arkan and Dragan?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: That is indeed what the documents I reviewed indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, that was your conclusion on the basis of all the documents you saw and relied upon in your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, going back to the first group, the tacit authorisation group, if I can refer to them as that, you include in that, and I want to try to be as specific as possible, the White Eagles, Dusan Silni, Srpska Garda, the Vuk Draskovic group, and the Serbian Chetnik movement SRS/SCP. And I'm looking at page 85 of part 1, and in e-court we need page 81.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's almost impossible because the numbering in e-court is usually higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This point was confusing me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So perhaps you should check that first.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, it's 108, e-court 108. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To answer the question, I mean, as I said in the executive summary it goes beyond tacit authorisation. There is also active support, and okay the names you have given I identify them as the best known volunteer/paramilitary groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So your conclusion is that the failure to abide by the duties placed upon the Serbian MUP led to tacit authorisation of every paramilitary group within the indictment frame?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Can you show me where I conclude that in my report?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, the -- the evidence you've just given is that the tacit authorisation related to the groups which are listed at paragraph -- on page 85, but also other groups. Am I misunderstanding you? I'm trying to get some specificity so I know what I'm dealing with over the next few days as to which groups you say were tacitly authorised by the failure of the Serbian MUP to fulfil its legal duties.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I mean, what -- what we see is that as I put it in the report, this is page 85 under title B, that a number of political parties in Republic of Serbia establish paramilitary groups, i.e., illegal groups or privately controlled groups that act in a military way with weapons and uniforms and participate in the fighting. Of course, over time efforts are done to legalise that situation on the field as well as in Serbia itself. On the field through establishment, for example, of operational groups and tactical groups, as well as other ad hoc units to ensure single authority. In Serbia we see that a number of -- I mean, that is discussed further on -- legal measures are taken. First of all we see that Article 118 --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, Mr. Theunens. I just want to keep us both focused if I can.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Okay, but I --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Which groups are we talking about that you say were tacitly authorised by the failures of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Maybe -- I have difficulties to understand your question, because you're moving to Serbian MUP groups, then you're going back to other groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me be clearer then if I can.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's put aside what you said about Dragan --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- Arkan and the Red Berets. Let's deal with all other paramilitary groups that you had in mind --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- when you concluded that the Serbian MUP's failures gave rise to tacit authorisation.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The -- I mean, the failure lays in the fact that the existing legislation --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm not asking you -- and we'll come to --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah, but I don't understand the question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We'll come to what the failures --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- may or may not have made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if the failures are part of your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then of course if the witness does not fully understand what you mean by that, then you should clarify that. So even if you want to go in further detail about the failures at a later stage, your question was whether the witness concluded that the Serbian MUP's failures gave rise to authorisation. So that needs an understanding of whether you, when you're talking about the failures, whether the witness understands what you mean, and I got the impression that he's trying to find out whether your understanding of the failure was exactly what --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether he understood well what you meant by the failure, and therefore wanted to expound a bit on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Mr. Theunens wants to, then I take Your Honour's point.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I mean, I will try my best to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Theunens. Maybe I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could try to assist both of you. The failure of the MUP, would that, as understood by Mr. Jordash, you can verify whether you have the same understanding, would that automatically include tacit -- what was the word?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Authorisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tacit authorisation. Is that what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can take you to the section in the report. Perhaps this is the best way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Then we go first to the failure and then to the -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Please could we go to paragraph -- sorry page 80 of part 1, and it is e-court 57. Sorry, it's 103. And the paragraph I'm concerned with, Mr. Theunens, is paragraph C.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "During the conflict in Croatia, nationalist political parties in Serbia were allowed to organise the recruitment, training, and dispatching of volunteers to the conflicts zones in Croatia or even set up their own volunteer paramilitary formations with the tacit authorisation of the government Republic of Serbia." Paragraph D: "The SFRY Supreme Command, the JNA, and the government of the Republic of Serbia, in particular the ministry of interior (MUP) and the ministry of defence (MOD), were aware of the existence of extra-legal volunteer/paramilitary formations participating in the conflict in Croatia and the role of nationalistic political parties in the recruitment of volunteers and encouraged these groups or supported them otherwise." Now, what I'm trying to clarify is which groups do you say were tacitly authorised and thereby encouraged by the failures of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. Now, I'm not in a position -- I wasn't able to identify which specific -- I mean, the name of the group, but we can say that these nationalistic parties established groups, and then as the government of the Republic of Serbia whereby the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of Interior have specific responsibilities in enforcing the law did not act against these groups as a whole. We know that later on there are selective actions against certain groups, but I cannot answer your question whether the Ministry of Interior specifically authorised group A or group B or group C. I also want to emphasise that this is a paragraph out of an executive summary which basically summarises what follows in the report --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, this isn't a part of the executive summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you would take the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's not the summary. It's page 80 of the first part.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Section 3, Mr. Theunens, labelled Serbian volunteers/paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's not [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, but it's -- [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I do agree we have two kind of summaries. We have the summary at the beginning of the report as a whole, and here we have a section 3 Serbian volunteers/paramilitaries starts with a summary of what then follows. Yes. So to that extent it is a summary, and therefore if Mr. Theunens could find where this is further explained at a later stage, he may include that in his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if we go to page 85 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, looking at the clock --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I noticed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's -- you've heard the question, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have a lot of time to think about an answer and to go through the report and find perhaps an answer in the part which is not a summary. I apologise, but you have several levels of summaries, and I first ignored that. Mr. Theunens, we'll continue tomorrow, but I'd first like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony either already given or still to be given tomorrow. If I say not to speak, that includes all kind of communication. Perhaps it would even be wise, knowing your background, to perhaps spend the evening in such a way that no one could even think of you discussing the matters with others. Therefore, we'd like to see you back tomorrow, and our schedule, as far as matters stand now for tomorrow, is that we start at 9.00 in the morning in this courtroom, II, until 11.30, and that in the afternoon we'll sit from 3.00 in the afternoon in Courtroom I, up to 6.00. We stand adjourned until tomorrow, Wednesday day, the 27th of October, 9.00, the same courtroom, II.
